title: The Killing form when the radical vanishes
statement:
The radical $\rad\mathfrak l$ of a Lie algebra $\mathfrak l$ is the sum of
all its solvable ideals. If $\rad\mathfrak l=0$, the Killing form
$B(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x\operatorname{ad}y)$ is
nondegenerate and $[\mathfrak l,\mathfrak l]=\mathfrak l$.

steps.text:
By invariance of $B$, the kernel $\mathfrak k$ of $B$ is an ideal. For
$x\in[\mathfrak k,\mathfrak k]$ and $y\in\mathfrak k$, the operators
$\operatorname{ad}x$ and $\operatorname{ad}y$ map $\mathfrak l$ into
$\mathfrak k$, and hence

$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak k}
(\operatorname{ad}(x)|_{\mathfrak k}\operatorname{ad}(y)|_{\mathfrak k})
=B(x,y)=0.
$$

By the trace criterion [sk-lem-walg-trace-criterion], the image of
$\mathfrak k$ in $\operatorname{End}(\mathfrak k)$ is solvable. The kernel
of $\mathfrak k\to\operatorname{End}(\mathfrak k)$ is the center of
$\mathfrak k$, which is abelian. Hence $\mathfrak k$ is a solvable ideal of
$\mathfrak l$, and therefore $\mathfrak k=0$. This proves that $B$ is
nondegenerate. By invariance and nondegeneracy, we have

$$
[\mathfrak l,\mathfrak l]^\perp=Z(\mathfrak l).
$$

Since the center is a solvable ideal, it is zero. Thus the derived algebra
has zero orthogonal complement, and hence it is all of $\mathfrak l$.
